text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A 12-year low in gold bullion prices on Friday with predictions of further falls has the Australian gold industry facing a crisis. The Reserve Bank's announcement it had sold two-thirds of Australia's gold holdings saw prices fall to $US322 an ounce in Lodon trade over the weekend, leaving more than half of Australia's gold mines uneconomic and facing closure. Page 1.

Base metals giant MIM Holdings Ltd is to cut production at its Mt Isa 1100 orebody from 4.4 million tonnes to 3.6 million tonnes a year in an attempt to improve costs but will maintain current copper production levels using existing slag stockpiles. MIM sokesman Collin Myers denied the cut in 1100 output was due to the operation having high production costs. Page 21.

Hawker Richardson managing director Graeme Salthouse has defended the company directors' quick decision to accept a A$1.86 a share offer from Austrim Ltd, and recommended shareholders accept the offer in the absence of a better one. Salthouse said the offer did not necessarily mean Hawker would disappear from the stock exchange boards. Page 21.

QCT Resources Ltd has warned that lower shipments, lower selling prices and the higher value of the Australian dollar have hurt the profitability of the company's coal mine interests for the last financial year. The company's annual coal shipments were slghtly higher than the previous year due to its increased interest in the Central Queensland Coal Associates and Gregory joint ventures. Page 23.

Allen Allen & Hemsley law firm partner Katherine Sainty has warned company directors they may be at risk of personal liability in millennium bug law suits. Sainty said the directors would be held responsible for all transactions affected by the problem, which would be caused by a glitch in older computers when the year 2000 will be interpreted as 1900. Page 27.

A hardline approach by Optus executives has lessened the enthusiasm at merger talks on Australia's pay-TV content, which will continue this week. Optus chief executive Peter Howell-Davies and chief operating officer Phil Jacobs have indicated they will seek to lead content negotiations. Page 29.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Mineral Policy Institute and the Australian Conservation Foundation have lodged a formal complaint with the Australian Securities Commission against Rio Tinto over claims the company misled shareholders in relation to the environmental and human right impact of the Grasberg copper and gold mine in Irian Jaya. Page 29.

Small Kalgoorlie gold miner Croesus Mining's chairman Ron Manners says the industry has been forced in to a constant state of defence by the native title process, arguments over the diesel fuel rebate, falling prices resulting from the Reserve Bank's announcement of its sale of two-thirds of its gold holdings, and the possibility WA will impose a Gold Royalty next year. Manners believes that gold companies may accelerate short-term production so they could move offshore. Page 29.

The Asian Infrastructure Fund intends to invest up to A$267 million next year to become a significant player in the deregulated telecommunications industry. AIF is a major shareholder in Spectrum Network Systems and WorldxChange Australia, and managing diector William Liley has suggested a merger of the two could increase their influence in the market. Page 29.

Building materials supplier James Hardie Industries' piping division is turning a profit after two and a half years of losses. The pipe division accounts for about 10 per cent of the company's A$1.5 billion annual turnover and the increased sales are a reflection of the construction industry's growth of eight per cent in the year to June. Page 31.

National Mutual Holdings' share price has risen by 15 per cent in the last month with shares trading above A$2. A broking analyst said the share price had tended to track the stock's appraisal value, but now that the company had profitability and a tradig history, investors were more willing to price the stock on an earnings per share basis. Page 31.

Woolworths managing director Reg Clairs said yesterday Asia's changing consumer patterns, and an increasing demand for Australian-produced food products, could see Australia become a global food supplier in the next three years. Analysts are predicting Wolworths to record a profit of $A255 million this year. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Qantas has experienced the fastest period of growth in its history over the past few years, with staff increasing by about 4000 and revenue up by 20 per cent. Shares in the company peaked at A$3.15 last week and a net profit is expected of A$250 million n the year to June. Page 37.

Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp chairman William Purves has suggested mergers between the four major Australian banks are inevitable, and has criticised the Federal Government for not accepting the proposal to remove restrictions on major bank mergers s detailed in the Wallis report. Page 37.

Stockbroking analysts predict that only gold companies with low development costs, long life mines, good management and strong forward sales to survive last week's gold price slump. Analysts say they could only recommend gold stocks that met all the critria. Page 37.

Suncorp-Metway is expected to announce fee increases of up to 150 per cent from today. Each withdrawal over four times in a month will cost the customer A$1.25, an increase of 75 cents. Using the ATMs of other banks will cost A$1, as will personal cheques Page 39.

Hungry Jack's, a subsidiary of Competitive Foods, is suing US company Burger King and Shell Australia for damages following a dispute over the opening of Hungry Jack's stores in Shell outlets, and to protect its rights concerning future Australian franchies. Under the current agreement, Competitive Foods could open a Hungry Jack's store if certain conditions were satisfied, but Burger King says it has ended the agreement because Competitive Foods breached several of the conditions. Page 39.

FAI Insurances Group will raise A$113 million in fresh equity to list a portfolio of office towers on the Australian Stock Exchange with FAI managing director Rodney Adler saying the company is holding too much property. The float will offer a yield of 905 per cent in its first year. Page 41.
THE AGE

Gold explorer Mt Kersey Mining's high-grade Silver Swan nickel project in Western Australia has just produced its first nickel concentrates. The group's market value of more than A$240 million is largely based on the exploration potential of tenements nea the Silver Swan project. Page B3.

A deal that did not proceed between Melbourne-based video rental chain Movieland and United States video company West Coast Entertainment has prompted Movieland to consider public listing to fund its expansion. Analysts believe a local listing could promp issues by other video rental operators. Page B3.

Jack Cowin's Hungry Jacks is suing US hamburger company Burger King and Shell Australia over a dispute over the opening of Hungry Jacks outlets in Shell service stations and to protect its rights over future franchises in Australia. Page B3.

It looks like a tough and long road for the gold stocks following the publication of the Reserve Bank's decision to dump its gold reserves. Junior explorers which rely on the market for exploration funding are particularly affected. Page B3.

Victorian Management Training Centre head Bronwyn Covill says McDonald's is revolutionising the concept of corporate training by pushing for accreditation at secondary and tertiary levels. McDonald's hopes to win MBA status for its executive development pogram and there are moves to gain Victorian Certificate of Education accreditation for junior courses. Page B3.

The magnetic stripe technology used on credit and debit cards will soon be replaced by the multi-application chip. The chip can form the basis of banking as well as acting as an airline ticket, boarding pass, the log on a frequent flier program and other key functions in daily life. Page B1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
